external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Each user belongs to one company and is either an admin or a viewer. They sign in with an email address and a password and get a session cookie.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The person who receives an invoice email and accesses the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: An agent who works from the support office network and uses the admin console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in to the admin console with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, which manages invoices, customer data, payout bank details, PDF jobs, and PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console reachable from the support office network that allows an agent to open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.source_excerpt: The admin console is reachable only from there

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A renderer that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes PDFs to the PDF bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The database has no row-level security and the app connects with one database account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue carrying PDF render jobs with a company ID and an invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared bucket where the PDF renderer writes PDFs under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time, reads the invoice from the tenant database and writes the PDF to the PDF bucket
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: Customer users use the billing app in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customer information, payout bank details, and account/session data

data_flows.name: edit invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user submits the whole invoice form to the billing app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The invoice edit form posts the whole invoice back
data_flows.notes: The billing app saves every field it receives, including the paid flag and the company's payout bank account.
data_flows.data_description: The whole invoice, including the paid flag and the company's payout bank account

data_flows.name: request PDF
data_flows.description: A user requests a PDF of an invoice.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.
data_flows.data_description: A request for a PDF identified by invoice number

data_flows.name: access tenant data
data_flows.description: The billing app reads and writes tenant data in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app adds the company filter to each query itself
data_flows.notes: The app connects with one database account for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customer information, payout bank details, company IDs, and invoice fields

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a PDF render job on the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue
data_flows.data_description: A company ID and an invoice number

data_flows.name: take render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
data_flows.data_description: A company ID and an invoice number

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads an invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID the job carries.
data_flows.data_description: An invoice selected using the company ID and invoice number from the job

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a PDF to the bucket under the company ID and invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_flows.data_description: A rendered invoice PDF, stored under a company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Invoice PDFs

data_flows.name: send invoice email
data_flows.description: The billing app sends the payer an invoice link ending in the invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: An invoice link ending in the invoice number

data_flows.name: open payment page
data_flows.description: The payer opens the payment page using the invoice link.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.notes: The payment page asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.data_description: A request for the invoice payment page

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code
data_flows.authentication: own account and a one-time code
data_flows.data_description: Account credentials and one-time code

data_flows.name: open customer session
data_flows.description: A support agent opens a billing-app session as any customer user through the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user, and not against the agent.
data_flows.authentication: admin-console session acting as any customer user
data_flows.data_description: A customer-user session and subsequent customer-user actions

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The tenant boundary for a customer company whose people use the invoicing service.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud platform in which the shared billing app, database, and PDF bucket operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents work and from which the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF renderer presents a non-web interface because it is described as a job-processing renderer that takes jobs from a queue.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the PDF renderer as taking jobs from the render queue one at a time, which supports classifying it as a non-web batch-style process.
